paraphrase: Original awakening (benjue) is the mind's nature free of thought, equal to space, the dharmakāya of the Tathāgata; because of it one speaks of non-awakening, and actualized awakening (shijue) is the return to it; when actualized awakening is complete it is identical with original awakening.
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge at chapter level; passage not read in a local text in this phase.

location.section: T1666, part 3 (解釋分), 顯示正義

paraphrase: The one mind has two aspects: the mind as suchness (xin zhenru), neither born nor perishing, the one dharmadhātu, which is 'empty' as free of all deluded marks and 'not empty' as full of pure qualities; and the mind as arising and ceasing, which depends on the tathāgatagarbha — the ālaya consciousness in which non-arising and arising combine.
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge at chapter level; passage not read in a local text in this phase.
